CBB More Auto Racing Entertainment Twitter Instagram Youtube Linkedin Texas vs. Oklahoma score prediction by expert football model: Who wins the Red River Shootout? By James Parks | October 7, 2026 One of college football’s great rivalry games renews this weekend as the Red River Shootout finds No. 1 ranked Texas facing off against Oklahoma in a critical test for both sides, if for very different reasons just a month into the 2026 season. Texas, still the class of the SEC , owns signature wins against Ohio State and Tennessee that catapulted it into the top AP ranking. Oklahoma fell out of the poll after falling to 2-2 and is once again facing structural questions around what remains a very anemic offense. What do the analytics department think of this week’s matchup? For that, let’s turn to the SP+ college football model to project the outcome, and use it to lock in our own prediction. Texas vs. Oklahoma score prediction: Can Arch Beat the Sooners' Defense? Sep 26, 2026; Knoxville, Tennessee, USA; Texas quarterback Arch Manning (16) celebrates after a college football game between Tennessee and Texas at Neyland Stadium in Knoxville, Tenn. on Sept. 26, 2026. Mandatory Credit: Brianna Paciorka-USA TODAY Network via Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) It may not come as a surprise that the Longhorns are getting the favorite treatment against the Sooners, and by a decent margin, too. SP+ predicts that Texas will defeat Oklahoma by a projected score of 27 to 17 and will win the game by an expected margin of 9.9 points in the process. The model gives the Longhorns a very strong 73 percent chance of victory, one of the biggest discrepancies of any game this weekend. SP+ is a “tempo- and opponent-adjusted measure of college football efficiency” that attempts to predict game outcomes by measuring “the most sustainable and predictable aspects of football.” How good is it this season? So far, the SP+ college football prediction model is 146-122-3 in its picks against the spread with a 54.4 win percentage. What actually happens? Can the Longhorns defend their No. 1 ranking? Sep 4, 2026; Norman, Oklahoma, USA; Oklahoma Sooners quarterback John Mateer (10) in action during the game against the UTEP Miners at Gaylord Family-Oklahoma Memorial Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Kevin Jairaj-Imagn Images That’s a different question. Even with a Texas win, its place atop the AP poll could be in danger anyway as pollsters may be more impressed with what happens between No. 2 Georgia and No. 6 Alabama as they face off in primetime. A big win over the Sooners could sway enough voters to stay at No. 1 , and everything looks like it should go the Longhorns’ way. Even with questions around Arch Manning’s continued development at the quarterback position. Sure, Texas is 4-0 and Manning looks much better than this time last year, but he has also clearly still not performed to expectations, either. Arch is a decent 63 percent passer but is making some curious decisions and doesn’t look completely at ease in the pocket against better-quality fronts. Against an Oklahoma defense that, despite everything, remains one of college football’s best – 4th against the pass, top 25 in scoring, and 3rd in third-down conversions – Manning could get seriously rattled early. But the Longhorns still have an advantage of their own on defense. They have battery of elite pass rushers who can wreck OU’s blockers, shrink the pocket, and get at John Mateer on a regular basis. That should give the Texas offense enough chances to separate and pull away late. Horns by 10. What happens? Texas beats Oklahoma, and covers the spread. away.headline: Texas Longhorns Receive Good and Bad News on First Injury Report vs. Oklahoma
away.blurb: Additionally, tight end Nick Townsend is probable after suffering a knee injury against Ohio State. He's missed the past two games. Fortunately, the Longhorns have a tight end room that features multiple contributors with Emaree Winston, Spencer Shannon and Michael Masunas. On top of that, Texas running back Hollywood Smothers is completely off the injury report. Texas gives injury non-update on Hollywood Smothers, Nick Townsend status once again Skip to main content Recruiting After nearly a week and a half since we last saw the Texas Longhorns take the field against the Tennessee Volunteers, many people were eager to hear how previously injured players had progressed over the bye. However, what should come as no surprise is that Texas head coach Steve Sarkisian had another idea in mind : no update. With star players like running back Hollywood Smothers, tight end Nick Townsend, and defensive lineman Justus Terry all missing time this season, Longhorn Nation has been eager to see their guys back in action. Unfortunately, we will have to wait to see what we should expect on Saturday. "I think we're healthier than we were a week ago at this time," Sarkisian said in his game preview press conference, continuing his refusal to share injury updates beyond what he puts in the SEC-mandated availability reports. Steve Sarkisian sticks to SEC availability report and nothing more On Monday of Week 4, before the Horns faced the Vols, Sarkisian expressed a similar sentiment, refusing to update members of the media on any lingering injuries, stating that "There's called an injury report in the SEC, so that's enough of the injury questions," Sarkisian said that week. Based on the final injury list from Texas's game against Tennessee, one could easily assume that Smothers will be good to go against the Oklahoma Sooners this weekend as the Horns prepare for the annual Red River Rivalry. The star running back was off the report just before kickoff and was seen on the sidelines in full pads, with his helmet on, but never entered the game against the Volunteers. However, when it comes to Terry and Townsend, your guess is as good as mine. Smothers is nursing a reported lower-leg injury suffered in practice, Townsend is healing up from a knee injury he sustained before Week 2's kickoff, Terry is recovering from a toe injury ahead of Week 2's game, Coleman hasn't played since Week 3, and Filsaime has yet to take the field this season. For right now, Texas fans (and Oklahoma fans) will have to wait to see what Texas's injury list looks like on Wednesday evening, because until then, Sarkisian is remaining tight-lipped about the health of his team. home.headline: Oklahoma vs Texas: Key players listed on Wednesday Availability report
home.blurb: Most notable is that the guy who was supposed to start at left tackle, Michael Fasusi, doesn't look like he'll be available again this week. He started for the Sooners against UTEP but has missed the last three games with a shoulder injury. Fasusi is doubtful for the Red River Showdown. Also in question is the status of starting left guard Eddy Pierre-Louis. Pierre-Louis was listed as questionable going into Saturday. Joining the ranks of the unavailable this week are Xavier Robinson and Jacobe Johnson. Johnson suffered an injury during the loss to Georgia. Why Robinson isn't available is anyone's guess. He didn't get much playing time against the Bulldogs, logging just three snaps after getting nine snaps the week before against Michigan. Along with Fasusi, who is doubtful, are reserve backup tight end Trynae Washington and backup offensive lineman Fred Hinton. Washington has been a piece of Oklahoma's short-yardage formations, lining up in the backfield as a fullback for the Sooners. Their presence on the availability report is just another week where the Sooners will have question marks along the offensive line. Names to watch as the week moves along include linebacker Cole Sullivan, wide receiver Jer'Michael Carter, safety Michael Boganowski, and tight end Jack Van Dorselaer. The Sooners need a spark this week if they want to keep their College Football Playoff hopes alive. The Sooners are 1-3 against the Texas Longhorns under Brent Venables, and the offense hasn't scored a touchdown against their Red River rivals since 2023. Missing key members of the offensive line and the tight end room doesn't bode well for the Sooners' chances this Saturday. Their running backs are as good as anyone who will go against them this year. They have a lot of players that came with them. And again, why I draw some comparisons to Indiana: a lot of guys that traveled with their coach right to the next stop.” First-year UCLA coach Bob Chesney brought offensive coordinator Dean Kennedy, defensive coordinator Colin Hitschler, and fifth-year running back Wayne Knight along with him to sunny California after the James Madison Dukes of the Sun Belt Conference made the College Football Playoff last season. Their memorable run came to an end in the first round after a 51-34 loss to the Ducks in the Pacific Northwest on Dec. 21, 2025. “Extremely well-coached team," Lanning continued on about this year's Bruins. picks.blurb: Greg McElroy Picks UCLA vs. Oregon Winner With Dante Moore's Status Unclear Skip to main content SI.COM TRANSFER PORTAL More from CFB-HQ On SI NEWS ESPN analyst Greg McElroy picked Oregon to beat unbeaten No. 21 UCLA on Saturday at Autzen Stadium, betting that the Ducks' run defense can contain first-year coach Bob Chesney's ground game whether Dante Moore or Dylan Raiola starts at quarterback. McElroy took the Ducks 31-21 on his Always College Football podcast and built the pick around a red-zone trend for Oregon coach Dan Lanning. "Dan Lanning is 39-1 in his career when Oregon gets more red-zone trips than the opponent," McElroy said. Who starts at quarterback for Oregon? Oregon quarterback Dylan Raiola throws a pass as the Oregon Ducks face the USC Trojans | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect Moore suffered a concussion in Oregon's 41-27 win at USC on Sept. 26, and he returned to practice Monday in a helmet and shoulder pads. Still, Lanning hasn't cleared the former UCLA quarterback, and the Big Ten's first injury report for the game is due Wednesday night. Moore suffered a concussion in Oregon's 41-27 win at USC on Sept. 26, and he returned to practice Monday in a helmet and shoulder pads. Still, Lanning hasn't cleared the former UCLA quarterback, and the Big Ten's first injury report for the game is due Wednesday night. Raiola replaced Moore at the Coliseum and went 19 of 25 for 289 yards and two touchdowns. However, McElroy pointed to the Nebraska transfer's history against ranked teams. "If you look back at his time at Nebraska, he was 0-5 against ranked football teams," McElroy said. "Well, UCLA is ranked." A Raiola start would also come one week before Oregon faces Nebraska. Wayne Knight vs. Oregon run defense UCLA running back Wayne Knight (3) looks on after scoring a touchdown during the second half against San Diego State | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect UCLA is 4-0 and 2-0 in the Big Ten after a 54-3 win at Maryland on Sept. 26. Chesney became the first UCLA coach since Red Sanders in 1949 to open his tenure 4-0 . UCLA is 4-0 and 2-0 in the Big Ten after a 54-3 win at Maryland on Sept. 26. Chesney became the first UCLA coach since Red Sanders in 1949 to open his tenure 4-0 . Running back Wayne Knight, who followed Chesney from James Madison , has 445 yards and nine touchdowns on 49 carries against FBS opponents. McElroy noted the Bruins average 7 yards per carry, the best mark in the country. But Oregon has allowed just nine runs of 10 or more yards. The Bruins' passing game is the concern. Quarterback Nico Iamaleava has thrown four touchdown passes, which McElroy said ranks 118th nationally, and Chesney's teams struggle when they have to lean on the pass. "Bob Chesney is 20-1 as an FBS head coach when his team runs fewer than 30 pass plays," McElroy said. "He is 1-3 when they have to throw it 40 or more times." Why did McElroy pick Oregon? Oregon Ducks head coach Dan Lanning runs out to the field with players before a game against the Portland State Vikings | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect McElroy expects Oregon to load up against the run and force Iamaleava to beat a defense that holds opponents to a 54% completion rate. McElroy expects Oregon to load up against the run and force Iamaleava to beat a defense that holds opponents to a 54% completion rate. "Oregon will completely sell out against the run," McElroy said. "So once the Bruins are forced to throw the ball, that's when the matchup starts to tilt pretty hard in the direction of the Ducks," McElroy added. UCLA's best upset path runs through turnovers. The Bruins are plus-8 in turnover margin, tied for third nationally, while Oregon has given the ball away twice all season. UCLA also averages 10 penalties per game, which McElroy said ranks 137th out of 138 teams, and that number becomes harder to overcome in a road environment like Autzen. History favors the Ducks, too. Oregon has won the last five meetings, and McElroy noted UCLA's last win in Eugene came in 2004, when Lanning was a freshman linebacker at William Jewell. McElroy picked against Oregon in Week 4, taking USC 34-31 before the Ducks won by 14 at the Coliseum. UCLA and Oregon kick off at 3:30 p.m. ET on CBS. Loading recommendations... picks.headline: Early preview of No. 23 UCLA Bruins ahead of Oregon Ducks showdown
picks.blurb: Early preview of No. 23 UCLA Bruins ahead of Oregon Ducks showdown - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Dodgers return to NLCS Rays sweep Yankees Brewers clinch NLCS Valkyries, Dream win Game 2s NFL Power Rankings Early preview of No. 23 UCLA Bruins ahead of Oregon Ducks showdown Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Oregon Ducks are in the midst of a much-needed bye week, enjoying some time off after a strenuous and pressure-filled first month of the 2026 season. Through four games, we've seen the Ducks start at No. 2 in the AP poll, drop to No. 6 after an underwhelming win over Boise State before losing to Oklahoma State, dropping them all the way down to No. 21. They then took care of Portland State, 84-0, moving them up a spot before a pivotal road matchup in Los Angeles with USC . The Ducks never blinked, even when quarterback Dante Moore had to leave the game via ambulance with a head injury, as backup Dylan Raiola and some timely defensive plays powered Oregon over USC, 41-27. It was as impressive of a win as we've seen from the Ducks over the past two seasons, and one that they badly needed in order to keep their goals of winning a national championship alive. Now, Oregon gets to take a breath and relax with a Week 5 bye. But that's not all that the players and staff are doing, as they'll be getting a jumpstart on preparing for the upstart UCLA Bruins , who will come to town in Week 6. We'll follow suit, providing an early deep-dive preview of how the Bruins ' season has gone so far, a breakdown of the offense, defense, special teams and players to watch with game and betting details to boot. Let's start with UCLA's resume, as they head into the matchup with Oregon looking to continue their undefeated season. UCLA's Resume Through Five Weeks Sep 26, 2026; College Park, Maryland, USA; UCLA Bruins wide receiver Aidan Mizell (1) dances in the end zone with wide receiver Landon Ellis (11) and wide receiver Semaj Morgan (4) after catching an 83-yard touchdown reception in the second half against the Maryland Terrapins at SECU Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Jamie Sabau-Imagn Images Week 1: W 45-24 @ Cal Week 2: W 28-10 vs. San Diego State Week 3: W 52-38 vs. Purdue Week 4: W 52-3 @ Maryland The Bruins got off to an impressive start in the newly-hired Bob Chesney era, taking down the Tosh Lupoi-led Golden Bears on the road after a dominant second half. Chesney, who commanded James Madison to the College Football Playoff a year ago, relied upon several of his former Dukes that followed him to Westwood in the season-opener. The start of the season was strong, and so was last game for UCLA. The Bruins went into Maryland and stomped all over the Terrapins, picking off four passes and racking up 475 total yards. The early, 10:30 PT start didn't hold them back, as they jumped out to a 20-3 lead at halftime and only added to the lead after the break. Sandwiched between those two spectacular outings were victories over San Diego State and Purdue, with the offense carrying them in the former and offense in the latter, showing how well-rounded the Bruins are in 2026. Offensive Breakdown Sep 26, 2026; College Park, Maryland, USA; UCLA Bruins running back Jaivian Thomas (21) celebrates with offensive line Hall Schmidt (65) after scoring a touchdown in the first half against the Maryland Terrapins at SECU Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Jamie Sabau-Imagn Images While last season was discombobulated at times for the Bruins offensively, new coordinator Dean Kennedy — coming over with Chesney from James Madison — has brought a revitalized, intelligent and, thus far, highly-successful offense to UCLA. Kennedy has a history of elevating previously subpar offensive units, as he developed quarterback Kyle Trask at Florida, turned Holy Cross into the Patriot League scoring leader and orchestrated the ninth-ranked scoring offense at James Madison in 2025. Now, he's doing the same thing at UCLA with a spread-based system that emphasizes physicality and explosiveness at the point of attack. Kennedy's units have consistently been among the best at creating explosive plays, both on the ground and through the air. While the Bruins won't go under center much at all, instead standing in the shotgun or pistol, they aren't afraid to run it right down the defense's throat. Through the air, the route combinations aren't necessarily complex, but they make it easy on the quarterback to read with a progression-based system. Defensive Breakdown Sep 26, 2026; College Park, Maryland, USA; UCLA Bruins linebacker Trent Hendrick (25) celebrates after intercepting a pass in the second half against the Maryland Terrapins at SECU Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Jamie Sabau-Imagn Images Also brought over from James Madison, Colin Hitschler is the defensive coordinator for the Bruins with a goal of instilling an uncommon physicality that hasn't been seen in Westwood for some time. And thus far this fall, UCLA has, for the most part, lived up those goals. The Bruins mostly operate out of a 4-2-5 defensive alignment, following the trend of opting to put an extra defensive back on the field over a lumbering linebacker. But make no mistake, the linebackers have plenty of talent to handle the middle of the field themselves, with a pair of seniors coming in at first and second on the team in tackles through four games. Hitschler isn't afraid to send pressure, having loads of success against Maryland in forcing the quarterback to make decisions under duress that turned into four interceptions. Expect more of the same come Week 6, with Hitschler putting the onus on the offensive line to protect whoever trots out at quarterback for the Ducks. Special Teams Breakdown Sep 12, 2026; Pasadena, California, USA; UCLA kicker Mateen Bhaghani (15) kicks a field-goal during the second half against San Diego State at the Rose Bowl. Mandatory Credit: William Liang-Imagn Images The Bruins have modest special teams units, with average kickoff and punt return marks with the same for the coverage units — though the return aspect could change in a blink with a pair of return men with elite speed waiting back there. In the kicking game, kicker Mateen Bhaghani has been solid in converting 4-of-5 field goals and all 23 extra points. It's his third season as the starter at UCLA, and he's made 82.8% of his field goals with a long of 57 yards — a massive advantage at the college level. Punter Curtis Gerrand also has a big leg, averaging 45.7 yards per punt on 15 boots thus far. Players to Watch Sep 26, 2026; College Park, Maryland, USA; UCLA Bruins quarterback Nico Iamaleava (9) passes in the first half against the Maryland Terrapins at SECU Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Jamie Sabau-Imagn Images There's an abundance of talent across the roster, yet these three players will have to be accounted for by the Ducks if they're to get their fourth win. QB Nico Iamaleava 2026 Season Stats: 62-for-99, 820 yards, 4 TDs, 2 INTs / / 35 rushes, 143 yards, 1 TD Analysis: Iamaleava hasn't quite needed to show off his world-class athleticism this year, with his backfield mate stealing much of the thunder in the first month of the season. That's not to say the former Tennessee starter can't scoot, as he's run for 1,077 yards and 11 touchdowns in four seasons while tossing 38 touchdowns and 14 interceptions. Not the most refined passer, Iamaleava — like many college quarterbacks — feasts on short and long throws, but hasn't quite developed the intermediate aspect of his game. Still very talented, Iamaleava is commanding mid-to-late round draft buzz, though he does have one more season of eligibility remaining. RB Wayne Knight 2026 Season Stats: 49 rushes, 445 yards, 9 TDs / / 8 catches, 88 yards Analysis: Yes, you read that right. Wayne has nine touchdowns four games into the year, with six coming in the first two games. Standing just 5-foot-7 and 193 pounds, Knight makes up for his lack of size with elite speed, vision and playmaking ability. At James Madison in 2025, Knight broke off runs of 73, 59, 58 and 49 yards with 57 and 49-yard gains on receptions. Always an ability to hit a home-run, the Ducks will have to be cognizant not to lose Knight behind the Bruins' offensive line. LB Sammy Omosigho 2026 Season Stats: 37 tackles, 3 sacks, 4 forced fumbles Analysis: Though the Bruins added 2025 Sun Belt Defensive Player of the Year Trent Hendricks to the roster recently, he's still getting acclimated so we'll spotlight Sammy Omosigho here. The 6-foot-2, 239-pound four-year Oklahoma transfer has gotten off to a fast start at UCLA, leading the team in tackles and recording three sacks from his linebacker spot. Hitschler sends the former Sooner quite often on pressures and he makes plays as evidenced by his four forced fumbles in four games. It will begin on Friday night when Iowa travels to the West Coast to take on Washington. The Huskies have dropped two games and would love to win over the No. 20 Hawkeyes. There is another big matchup brewing for 3:30 p.m. ET Saturday between No. 21 UCLA vs. No. 13 Oregon . It doesn't sound like Dante Moore will suit up for the Ducks, but Oregon will look to add another ranked win to its resume. Here's how every Big Ten game could play out this weekend. MORE: College Football Big Ten power rankings entering Week 6 No. 7 Indiana vs. Nebraska NCAA Football: Indiana at Rutgers Indiana Hoosiers quarterback Josh Hoover (10) looks back after throwing a touchdown pass during the first half against the Rutgers Scarlet Knights at SHI Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Vincent Carchietta-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Indiana is doing what most people thought it would do. The Hoosiers don't have a blemish on the 2026 season , and quarterback Josh Hoover appears to have exorcised his interception woes that haunted him during his TCU years. Meanwhile, Nebraska is doing more than people thought. Despite losing quarterback Dylan Raiola to Oregon, the Huskers are 5-0 and have the No. 3 rushing attack of all Big Ten teams this season. Transfer Antony Colandrea is a good dual-threat quarterback, and freshman Jamal Rule has led the Nebraska rushing attack with 333 yards, despite being banged up. This game is in Lincoln and Nebraska will have to run the ball to win. But IU has the No. 1 rushing defense in the Big Ten, allowing fewer than 65 yards per game on the ground. This will be the first game Nebraska falls. Final score: Indiana 31, Nebraska 20 No. 21 UCLA vs. No. 13 Oregon Oregon quarterback Dylan Raiola celebrates a touchdown by Oregon running back Dierre Hill Jr. as the Oregon Ducks face the USC Oregon quarterback Dylan Raiola celebrates a touchdown by Oregon running back Dierre Hill Jr. as the Oregon Ducks face the USC Trojans on Sept. 26, 2026, at Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum in Los Angeles, California. Credit: USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Bob Chesney has really turned UCLA around in a hurry. The Bruins are one of the pleasant surprises in college football, and he has UCLA 4-0 with a major game this weekend. James Madison transfer Wayne Knight is second in the Big Ten, averaging over 111 yards on the ground. UCLA might have some good news. Quarterback Dante Moore won't play this weekend, which sets up backup Raiola to start. While facing the backup is a good thing, Raiola is no typical backup. He started the last two seasons at Nebraska, and came in against USC and played well. The Ducks are loaded with playmakers, and all Raiola has to do is run the offense. The Bruins are a feel-good story, but Oregon has turned a corner and will be tough to beat in Eugene. Final score: Oregon 38, UCLA 27 No. 19 USC vs. Penn State NCAA Football: Washington at Southern California USC Trojans quarterback Jayden Maiava (14) looks to pass the ball against the Washington Huskies during the second half at United Airlines Field at Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum. Mandatory Credit: Griffin Hooper-Imagn Images via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Both of these teams are at a crossroads, but for different reasons. USC is supposed to be a College Football Playoff team in 2026, but a typical loss to Oregon has the Trojans on the brink. Another loss could push USC out of contention. As for Penn State, it had the most favorable schedule in the Big Ten, and head coach Matt Campbell had an outside chance to contend for a Big Ten title in Year 1. However, PSU has dropped the last two games against Wisconsin and Northwestern to move to 3-2 on the season. A .500 start is staring right at Penn State. When you look at these wo teams, there is a path for either to win, but USC is playing like the better team, and we've yet to see Penn State bounce back under its new staff. White Out or not, the Trojans get a big win. Final score: USC 30, Penn State 28 The rest of the games will be quick-hitter style: Washington 20, No. 20 Iowa 17 Northwestern 38, Ball State 7 Illinois 27, Michigan State 20 No. 5 Ohio State 41, Maryland 10 Minnesota 24, Purdue 17

It’s the first ranked Big Ten opponent to visit Eugene this season. The Ducks’ biggest question is at quarterback. Dante Moore (926 yards, nine touchdowns, 69.7% completions) suffered a concussion on a targeting hit in the 41-27 win at USC and remains in concussion protocol with no set return date. If Moore can’t go, former Nebraska starter Dylan Raiola gets the start. Raiola took over at USC and led Oregon to points on six of seven drives. Dan Lanning has said the team is taking “an abundance of caution” with Moore. Whoever starts will face one of the most opportunistic defenses in the country. Defensive coordinator Colin Hitschler’s 3-3-5 stack moves after the snap, and UCLA leads the Big Ten with eight interceptions. Six different Bruins have an interception, led by Ta’Shawn James with three, and UCLA is tied for the conference lead with five forced fumbles. The Bruins also have plenty of motivation. First-year coach Bob Chesney brought his James Madison team to Autzen last season and lost 51-34 after falling behind 34-6 at halftime. Ten former Dukes are on his first UCLA roster. Quarterback Nico Iamaleava is averaging a career-high 8.3 yards per play, and the Bruins scored 52 points against Purdue and 54 at Maryland in back-to-back weeks. picks.headline: 4 bold predictions as Oregon football looks for ranked win vs. UCLA
picks.blurb: News Sports Opinion Entertainment Real Estate Advertise Obituaries eNewspaper Legals FOOTBALL 4 bold predictions as Oregon football looks for ranked win vs. UCLA Alec Dietz Eugene Register-Guard Updated Oct. 7, 2026, 12:40 p.m. PT Just two weeks following an emotional, gut-check win over USC in Los Angeles, the Oregon football team will look to take down UCLA on Oct. 10 in Eugene . The Ducks (3-1, 1-0 Big Ten) were idle last week in their only bye of the season and take on a Bruins ' (4-0, 2-0) squad in the same position. "UCLA is playing a high level of ball," coach Dan Lanning said. "It's a coaching staff that we have a really high level of respect for." The game will kick off at 12:30 p.m. Saturday and air on CBS. Here's what to look for ahead of the ranked matchup. Oregon vs. UCLA scouting report Why Oregon has an advantage: The Ducks are the only team in the country to average over 300 passing yards per game without an interception, split between starter Dante Moore and backup Dylan Raiola. Oregon ranks third nationally in passing yards per game and has done a good job of avoiding turnovers. If the Ducks can dictate tempo through the air, create explosive plays and avoid turnovers, they should win this game. Why UCLA has an advantage: The Bruins, to this point in the season, have run the ball much more consistently than the Ducks. UCLA ranks in the top five nationally in rush yards per play, rushing touchdowns and rushing yards per game. Led by standout back Wayne Knight, the Bruins average nearly 7 yards per carry. The Ducks rank toward the back half in the country around 4.6 yards per rushing attempt. If the Bruins can establish their ground game and control the tempo of this game, they'll have a chance to spring an upset. Oregon vs. UCLA injury updates For Oregon: The main storyline for the Ducks this week will likely be the health of starting quarterback. After suffering a concussion against USC, Moore returned to practice this week, but his status moving forward is unclear. Oregon's first mandatory injury report will be released Wednesday night and should offer clarity on his availability moving forward. Elsewhere, receiver Jeremiah McClellan is expected to be out still while Jalen Lott could make his return after a hand surgery sidelined him through Oregon's first four games. For UCLA: The Bruins' injury report will also be released Wednesday night, but several banged-up players made their returns in UCLA's last outing against Maryland in Week 4. Receiver Aidan Mizell, DB Jhase McMillan and tight end Josh Phifer were all listed as questionable or probable and shifted to available on game day. Safety Tao Johnson, a starter, could make his return after an upper-body injury in Week 1. Oregon vs. UCLA: 4 bold predictions Oregon needs to run the ball, much better than it has, to win Outside of a record-breaking outing against a completely outclassed opponent in Portland State, the Ducks haven't run the ball nearly as well as they typically have under Lanning. If you take out Oregon's 84-0 win over PSU, it is only rushing for roughly 115 yards per game, which would rank near the bottom of the country. The Bruins are one of the top rushing teams in the country. Though Oregon's offense has been able to move the ball effectively through the air, it will absolutely need to run the ball better than it has to beat the Bruins. Quarterback play will determine winner Through four games, Oregon's quarterback play has not been a major issue. Moore has been effective and avoided turnovers while Raiola stepped in masterfully to deliver a satisfying win over USC. That, obviously, needs to continue this Saturday, but the play of UCLA quarterback Nico Iamaleava might just determine how this game plays out. The previously maligned former five-star quarterback had a season to forget in 2025 but has been more effective in 2026. Still, the emphasis for Oregon all week will be on stopping the run, meaning Iamaleava will have opportunities to make plays throughout the game. If he can take advantage and outduel whoever starts at QB for Oregon, UCLA will be in the driver's seat to win. Oregon will play its best game of the season vs. UCLA Though the Ducks are 3-1, Lanning himself admitted during the bye week that they are nowhere near where they want to be. USC was a big step forward in multiple facets, but the defense has some lingering issues and the offense still has things to figure out. Saturday's game will be Oregon's best effort of the season, following a recalibrating bye week. Still feeling the urgency from the Oklahoma State loss in Week 2, getting back in front of fans at Autzen Stadium will energize the Ducks, who will roar out to a double-digit win this Saturday in Eugene. home.headline: Oregon injuries could force Dan Lanning to address the Ducks’ biggest defensive issue
home.blurb: On Wednesday Night, the first injury report of the week was released for the matchup between the Oregon Ducks and the UCLA Bruins. While everyone was concerned about the status of Dante Moore, and for good reason as he'll be out, there were also several other notable players with a status on the report. Among the most notable mentions is starting safety Aaron Flowers who's listed as doubtful. Oregon may finally experiment with new safety looks with Aaron Flowers doubtful Trey McNutt is another player the fanbase would love to see, but based on the limited time he's played in games like the Portland State game, it's hard to see him vaulting up the depth chart into a big role. Oregon must improve in 3 areas coming out of the bye to beat UCLA Given that Aaron Flowers is in his second year as a starter at safety, the Ducks may be heading into this game without an experienced piece in the secondary. While Oregon may be down a starter, it may force the staff to try fixing a hole in the defense. One of the biggest issues for the Oregon defense early in the season has been the fact that the safety play has not been up to par. The Ducks added the top ranked safety in the Transfer Portal Koi Perich to plug the hole left behind by Dillon Thieneman, but the position hasn't been a strength like it was last season. Koi Perich has looked lost in coverage at times while he hasn't been nearly as effective as Thieneman in run support. Aaron Flowers has seemingly taken a step back after playing alongside an elite safety last year, and he hasn't helped the Ducks struggles' on the back end. If Aaron Flowers isn't able to play against UCLA, Oregon fans may finally get what they've wished for with a shakeup at the safety position. Oregon has stacked elite recruiting classes under Dan Lanning, and there's truly no shortage of talent at the position. The most likely safety to jump into a bigger role if Aaron Flowers misses time is veteran Peyton Woodyard. In the USC game with Flowers exiting with an upper body injury, Woodyard outsnapped the starter for the first time all season, and it may lead to a change moving forward. Woodyard played a much better game vs the Trojans than Flowers, and with his experience on this team, he may be the best option. The player the fanbase wants to see the most is 5-star freshman Jett Washington who did play 4 snaps vs. USC. Washington flashed his potential in the Portland State game with a pair of diving interceptions, and the talent is clearly through the roof. Thrusting Washington into a massive role in a pivotal game for the Ducks may be a massive risk, but we'll likely start to see his snap counts rise week over week, especially if Flowers is sidelined. (Photo by Ali Gradischer/Getty Images) Getty Cole Sullivan Wed, October 7, 2026 at 11:10 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads The No. 13 Oregon Ducks enter this Saturday coming off a bye week and gearing up for a top-25 matchup in Eugene against the No. 21 UCLA Bruins. Entering the showdown, the status of Oregon star quarterback Dante Moore, who sustained a scary concussion two weeks ago against the USC Trojans, has been one of the key question marks facing the Ducks. On Wednesday, however, it seems there's much more clarity on his status for Saturday's game. Oregon Receives Injury Update on Moore The Ducks turned to experienced backup Dylan Raiola after Moore exited the USC game, and he completed 19-of-25 passes for 289 yards and two touchdowns while leading the Ducks to a 41-27 victory. The Ducks appear ready to start Raiola again Saturday, while they likely won't play Moore even though they don't consider his injury overly serious. The team is taking extra precautions with its star quarterback. Via Matt Zenitz of CBS Sports : "Oregon star QB Dante Moore is currently considered unlikely to play against No. 21 UCLA this weekend as he continues to work back from the concussion he suffered vs. USC. "Leaves Dylan Raiola as the likely starter vs. UCLA. On a positive note with Moore, continues to practice and continues to progress working back from the concussion." The Ducks lost an early-season game to Oklahoma State, and while that loss doesn't look quite as bad given how Oklahoma State has come along, they're still entering every game with a must-win mindset, and their schedule certainly isn't an easy one. They still have games against surging Nebraska and Northwestern teams, No. 5 Ohio State on Nov. 7, and Michigan and Michigan State before closing the season against rival Washington. home.blurb: BATON ROUGE — LSU football' s initial injury report for this weekend's game at Kentucky is out. For the first time this season, there are no surprises on the report for Lane Kiffin and the Tigers (4-1, 1-1 SEC). LSU does not have any players listed as probable, questionable or doubtful on the report released Wednesday, Oct. 7 by the SEC. TREY'DEZ GREEN INJURY UPDATE Trey'Dez Green injury update: LSU tight end 'getting closer' to return Weeks and Green have not been ruled out for the rest of the season but have suffered leg injuries that will keep them out for a substantial amount of time. The No. 10-ranked Tigers face No. 25 Kentucky (4-1, 1-1) inside Kroger Field on Saturday, Oct. 10 (6 p.m. CT, ESPN). LSU VS KENTUCKY CFP IMPLICATIONS Why recent CFP history tells us that LSU's game vs Kentucky is crucial for playoff chances As expected, star linebacker Whit Weeks, tight end Trey'Dez Green , safety Dashawn Spears, as well as reserves and special teams players Charles Ross II and receiver Phillip Wright Jr., are on the list. Spears, Ross and Wright have suffered season-ending injuries. Weeks fractured his fibula against Texas A&M on Sept. 26 and has had a successful surgery to correct it. Green sprained his knee in the Ole Miss game and has missed the past two games for LSU. But earlier this week, Kiffin said the tight end was getting closer to playing. home.blurb: The LSU Tigers return to SEC play this weekend against the Kentucky Wildcats, which means another week of official injury reports to prepare for the week. While the first couple of weeks of reports brought chaos and some disappointing news, this is a pretty chill week for the Tigers (less so for the Wildcats). Here are the initial reports put out by the conference : No news is good news for LSU. They have five players ruled out, but all were expected to be out. There was nothing unexpected here. It is good to see the cornerback depth improving, with Ja'Keem Jackson off the report entirely. It is a long list for Kentucky this week, but nothing completely detrimental. They do have five players already listed out, the same as the Tigers, but only one was a Week 1 starter. Their depth has been completely wiped out, which could always come into play as well. LB Antwan Smith LB Alex Afari Jr. LB Tavion Wallace DB Jaden Smith DB Grant Grayton RB Jordan Colbert LS Cole Marszalek DL Kalen Edwards The best news for the Wildcats comes in the fact that running back Jason Patterson and defensive back Aaron Gates are not on the report. Patterson has been a key piece of their offense and left the game early against the South Carolina Gamecocks, so he was uncertain for this one. It looks like he'll be fully healthy. Gates is a high-potential player who has dealt with injuries that have hampered him throughout most of his career. He missed last week, but is their starting slot corner when healthy. That's an important role against this Lane Kiffin offense. home.headline: Cal GM Ron Rivera on Jaron-Keawe Sagapolutele Injury vs. UNLV: It Was `Avoidable'
home.blurb: The Bears (2-3, 1-1 ACC) return home Saturday to face Virginia Tech (3-2, 1-1) in a 12:30 p.m. kickoff at Memorial Stadium. Will JKS miss his first game in two seasons or could he return to face the Hokies? We don’t know. Turns out Sagapolutele continued to show “some symptoms” during the second half and he now is among four Cal players undergoing multiple tests every day as part of the Bears’ concussion protocol program. Safety Kingston Lopa is also facing those protocols, Lupoi said. Besides Lopa going out with the head injury, the Bears played portions of the UNLV game without defensive backs Cam Sidney and Daniel Harris, both ejected after targeting penalties. Cal GM Ron Rivera on Jaron-Keawe Sagapolutele Injury vs. UNLV: It Was `Avoidable' Skip to main content SI.COM Quarterback Jaron-Keawe Sagapolutele is among 10 Cal starters dealing with injuries — one of four in concussion protocol — coach Tosh Lupoi reported Tuesday. Cal is not required to provide details about injuries, although we will get status updates when the ACC releases its initial player availability chart on Wednesday night. We do know this much: Cal football athletic director and general manager Ron Rivera was not happy with the play that led to Sagapolutele leaving the game in the final minute of the half at UNLV. Rivera called the injury “avoidable.” Cal was trailing 24-7 when JKS rolled right and threw incomplete on first-and-10 from his own 25-yard line. UNLV linebacker Elias Rudolph, a transfer from Miami, flung Sagapolute to the artificial turf and the sophomore QB’s head bounced off the artificial turf. No flag was thrown, but Rivera clearly believed that should have happened. “JKS’s concussion, in my opinion, was avoidable. And I agree with Tosh, something should have happened,” he said. “When the quarterback throws the ball and the defender sees him throw the ball, there’s no reason to allow him to violently grab a guy and swirl around him and throw him to the ground. "Just go back and watch the tape. That’s all I’m going to say about that.” Lupoi removed Sagapolutele from the game after watching him stagger back to the huddle. At halftime, he was told JKS was cleared to play, but Lupoi said he didn’t feel comfortable sending him back onto the field. With backup Jackson Brousseau performing well at quarterback, Cal rallied to take a 25-24 lead in the second half before the Rebels answered to win 39-31. The closest Lupoi came to providing a hint as to whether Sagapolutele might face Virginia Tech was when he offered, “He was cleared to go back in at one point. That tells you it was a minor whatever-you-want-to-call-it.” Cal already has been playing without injured running backs Adam Mohammed and Carter Vargas. The Bears were desperate enough at the position that wide receivers Tyree Sams and Carson Perry-Smith were given snaps — and carries — at running back in Saturday. “You may or may not see that this week,” Lupoi said. home.headline: Cal Football Game Summary: Bears Lose to UNLV; Sagapolutele Injured
home.source: California Golden Bears On SI on MSN
home.blurb: Cal was without quarterback Jaron-Keawe Sagapolutele for the entire second half after he left the game in the final minute of the second quarter when he hit his head hard on the turf. He reportedly was cleared to return but Cal opted not put him back in the game with a head injury. Cal safety Kingston Lopa left the game with an injury three minutes into the first quarter and did not return. Bears starting nickel back Cam Sidney was ejected from the game for targeting in the first quarter. Cal defensive back Daniel Harris was ejected for targeting in the fourth quarter. INDIVIDUAL STAT OF THE GAME II: Cal limited all-Mountain West running back Jai'Den "Jet" Thomas to 46 yards on 16 carries. This game was considered a tipping point for Cal’s season, and it tipped the wrong way. Cal’s second straight loss reduces Cal’s chances to finish the season with a winning record for the second straight season. Before the season began, a 4-1 Cal record after five games seemed possible and a 5-0 start was not out of the question. A 2-3 mark at this stage was not what Cal supporters had in mind. The Bears have little momentum heading into the heart of its ACC schedule, which starts next Saturday with a home game against Virginia Tech. The outside complaints from Cal fans will continue, and the Bears are on the verge of becoming irrelevant this season. Cal rallied from a 24-7 halftime deficit to take the lead, but ultimately the Bears lost to UNLV 39-31 on Saturday afternoon at Allegiant Stadium in Las Vegas. Jackson Brousseau was the Bears' quarterback in the second half. Cal played the game without injured running back Adam Mohammed, the team’s leading rusher with 336 yards. RECORDS: CAL (2-3, 1-1 ACC), UNLV (3-2, 1-0 Mountain West) UNLV quarterback Jackson Arnold. Although he passed for just 158 yards, he threw touchdown passes of 70, 36 and 10 yards and ran for a 55-yard touchdown. He also had a key 42-yard run and finished with 110 rushing yards. With Cal leading 25-24, UNLV quarterback Jackson Arnold ran 42 yards to the Cal 12-yard line, which led to Arnold's 10-yard touchdown pass for a 32-25 UNLV lead with 9:38 left. KEY PLAY 1: On a fourth-and-2 play from the UNLV 47-yard line, Jaron-Keawe Sagapolutele completed a pass to Tyree Sams, but it was a half-yard short of a first down. It turned the ball over the UNLV with 12:20 left in the first quarter with the game scoreless. KEY PLAY 2: Cal safety Kingston Lopa, who leads the nation in interceptions with five, left the game with an injury three minutes into the first quarter. KEY PLAY 3: Sagapolutele completed a 91-yard touchdown pass to freshman tight end Taimane Purcell, who covered most of the ground himself. It gave Cal a 7-0 lead with 11:30 remaining in the first quarter. KEY PLAY 4 : Cal starting safety Cam Sidney was ejected for targeting with 11:25 left in the first quarter. KEY PLAY 5: On a third-and-8 play from the UNLV 30-yard line, Rebels quarterback Jackson Arnold completed a 70-yard touchdown

Entering the game, the matchup looks pretty even, with both teams having a real chance to take home the win. But according to ESPN's game predictor , Alabama has a slightly bigger opportunity to get the victory. Alabama has been given a 52.6 percent chance to take down Georgia, showing some of the slimmest of margins coming into the game. Part of why the Crimson Tide may be favored here is because the game is being played in Tuscaloosa. The Crimson Tide are very tough to beat at home, but Georgia is one of the few teams that has the talent to make it happen. Alabama will need to make sure that they bring their A-game into this matchup; otherwise, it could be a long night for everyone involved. Quarterback Keelon Russell is going to be tested in ways that he hasn't been so far this season, and he will need to prove that he can step up for the team. For Alabama to reach its big goals of winning a title this year, Russell is going to have to take on teams like Georgia while performing at a high level. But so far this year, Russell has passed all his tests with flying colors, entering his name into the Heisman Trophy conversation . If Russell can have another strong game against the Bulldogs, Alabama would likely be put in a good spot to grab the win at home. This is a measuring stick game for both teams, and the winner will have the upper hand to get into the College Football Playoff . One of the biggest features of GameDay is the "celebrity guest picker," which is usually a celebrity or athlete with ties to the university hosting GameDay. This season's guest pickers have featured the likes of Morgan Freeman and Lainey Wilson. While it is anyone's guess, here are five options for the GameDay guest picker in Tuscaloosa this Saturday. Bryce Young, NFL quarterback Sep 20, 2026; Atlanta, Georgia, USA; Carolina Panthers quarterback Bryce Young (9) looks to pass during the second quarter against the Atlanta Falcons at Mercedes-Benz Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Dale Zanine-Imagn Images The 2021 Heisman Trophy winner and 2023 No. 1 overall NFL draft pick, Bryce Young is one of the greatest quarterbacks in Alabama history. Young has been one of the top quarterbacks in the NFL this season. Young also has history with Georgia, having played against the Bulldogs in the 2021 SEC Championship Game in which he threw for 421 yards, as well as the 2021 CFP national championship. The Panthers have their bye week this upcoming weekend, which opens up the door schedule-wise for Young to potentially be the guest picker. Oba Femi, WWE superstar Oba Femi is introduced during WWE Friday Night SmackDown at Paycom Center in Oklahoma City, Friday, July 10, 2026. 28-year old WWE phenom Oba Femi, born Isaac Odugbesan , could be a strong option for ESPN if they opt to do some cross-promotion. ESPN currently owns the United States broadcast rights to WWE "premium live events" where Femi has become a fan-favorite with his patented entrance strut and powerful pro-wrestling style. Femi was a shot-put thrower at Alabama from 2019-22 where he was a two-time SEC Indoor conference champion. Femi toured the Alabama football facilities prior to the season, and was also featured on the "Paul Finebaum Show" at that time. Julio Jones, retired NFL wide receiver Dec 22, 2019; Atlanta, Georgia, USA; Atlanta Falcons wide receiver Julio Jones (11) warms-up before their game against the Jacksonville Jaguars at Mercedes-Benz Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Jason Getz-USA TODAY Sports One of the greatest wide receivers of all time, Julio Jones holds a key spot in Alabama history as arguably the player that helped turn Alabama into a wide receiver factory. Having one of the premier players of the last couple decades would be a smart decision for GameDay. Jones also has history with Georgia as he went for five catches, 94 yards, and a touchdown in Alabama's 41-30 win over Georgia in the infamous Georgia blackout game in Athens during his freshman season in 2008. Jones is also set to feature in the Nick Saban documentary that ESPN is putting out, of which the first episode of is set to be released on Thursday . Alabama right tackle Jayvin James is not featured on the initial availability report. James left the Sept. 26 home win over South Carolina early with a lower extremity injury, and it forced him to sit out of the Mississippi State victory. Nevertheless, DeBoer said during Monday's press conference that he's "optimistic that [James] can return this week." Looks like he's good to go. TUSCALOOSA, Ala. — The Southeastern Conference implemented a policy in 2024 that requires mandatory injury reports for football, basketball and baseball ahead of all conference games. However, it is only required for conference matchups. No. 6 Alabama football will play its fourth SEC game of the 2026 season at home against No. 2 Georgia on Saturday, Oct. 3, at 6:30 p.m. CT . Alabama tight end Josh Ford broke his arm during the Mississippi State. We’ve just got to make sure he meets the levels that we need him to meet as far as being physically ready. He's doing a great job. It's going well." I know where his mindset is at. We just got to make sure he meets the levels we need him to meet as far as being physically ready. He's doing a great job. It's going well. We're optimistic." Edmonds, a five-star freshman, has not played in a game after suffering a lower body injury in training camp. Alabama is scheduled to kick off against Georgia at 6:30 p.m. Saturday. home.headline: Did early season injuries help build Alabama’s offensive line depth?
home.blurb: “It’s great to see Tyrell get out there,” DeBoer said. “Tyrell is crazy athletic, has a lot of skill. And for him to get out there and get his feet underneath of him, I thought he did a nice job for his first, really, start, really from a volume standpoint, his most meaningful full reps. “There’s a high ceiling for him, for sure, and you can see that. He’s worked a couple of different positions, because throughout the year, throughout camp, we knew that he had that in him. But you’re also trying to get him just settled in on one position and be really good at one spot. But got out there and did a nice job.” Alabama football’s offensive line appears as if it will be at full strength for Saturday’s matchup with Georgia . Right tackle Jayvin James was not listed on the first availability report for the game Wednesday, after he missed the Crimson Tide’s trip to Mississippi State. That’s a positive for UA. However, against the Bulldogs, Tyrell Miller got his first college start. Even if he doesn’t get another this season, getting that experience could be huge down the stretch for the Tide, when depth becomes important late in the year. On Monday, Alabama offensive coordinator Ryan Grubb praised Miller’s effort. “I was proud of him,” Grubb said. “You know, I know the unit was excited. We kind of celebrated that a little bit on Friday night. You know, his first start, major college football, coming from JuCo program, and really only playing football for about three years now. So just seeing his ascension and the type of player he’s already become, but a lot of learning you know moments for him as well. “He gave up a sack. He saw the pressure coming off the edge. You know, just didn’t use clean enough footwork and end up giving up one there, and I know those are lessons that for Tyrell, they’re expensive in the moment, but for him down the road, I know he’ll utilize all that, realize the speed of the game, how much quicker it’s going. But he played well. He had some really critical blocks.” Miller joined Alabama this offseason, transferring in from the junior college level. He began his college career at College of San Mateo in California, after mostly focusing on basketball in high school. Speaking Monday, DeBoer also spoke positively of Miller. Miller isn’t the only Alabama OL backup to see time this season. Mal Waldrep has also played serious snaps at guard, especially when Will Sanders has been injured. Sanders and Waldrep battled for the starting spot on the left side all offseason. Waldrep might not have won the job, but he has provided crucial depth. “Mal brings a physicality,” DeBoer said. “Even though he’s younger, he brings a physicality that I think has helped our team. He’s got a kind of a no-nonsense approach. He’s what you want in an offensive lineman.” Entering the teeth of its SEC schedule, Alabama now has two backups on the offensive line who have gotten on the field. home.blurb: For the initial post, players are listed as “probable,” “questionable,” “doubtful,” or “out” on the injury report. Then, on game day, to provide further clarity, players will be designated as a “game-time decision,” or “out” for the upcoming game. If a player is removed from the report, then they are officially available for the game. This story will be updated throughout the week leading up to game time. Alabama right tackle Jayvin James is not featured on the initial availability report. James left the Sept. 26 home win over South Carolina early with a lower extremity injury, and it forced him to sit out of the Mississippi State victory. Nevertheless, DeBoer said during Monday's press conference that he's "optimistic that [James] can return this week." Looks like he's good to go. TUSCALOOSA, Ala. — The Southeastern Conference implemented a policy in 2024 that requires mandatory injury reports for football, basketball and baseball ahead of all conference games. However, it is only required for conference matchups. No. 6 Alabama football will play its fourth SEC game of the 2026 season at home against No. 2 Georgia on Saturday, Oct. 3, at 6:30 p.m. CT . Alabama tight end Josh Ford broke his arm during the Mississippi State. DeBoer said during Wednesday's teleconference that even though Ford received arm surgery this past Sunday, DeBoer is optimistic about him playing against Georgia. "Actually, progressing along fairly well right now," DeBoer said . "We'll kind of see how the week continues for him, and I know where his mindset's at. We’ve just got to make sure he meets the levels that we need him to meet as far as being physically ready. He's doing a great job. It's going well." Edge rushers Justin Hill and Desmond Umeozulu have missed the Crimson Tide's past two games. Hill has a lower-extremity injury and Umeozulu has turf toe. Hill and Umeozulu are the second and third Wolf linebackers on Alabama's depth chart. DeBoer shared the latest on these two as well, stating that Umeozulu will take "probably a couple more weeks," and Hill will "be back this season, but more than likely not this week." It was reported a couple of weeks before the season that 5-star freshman cornerback Jorden Edmonds would miss some time due to a lower body injury. DeBoer said on Monday that "there’s a chance he can come back here, even in a regular season." Fellow freshman (JUCO) defensive back Nick Sherman, who is also on the report, will also have to wait to make his debut, as he sustained an injury during a fall scrimmage. Jeremiah Beaman and Cayden Jones are also featured on the availability report, and they will both miss the 2026 season. Beaman tore his ACL during practice about two weeks before the season opener. Beaman tore his ACL in Week 1 of the 2025 season as well. DeBoer shared the news on Sept. 21 regarding Jones, but didn't reveal the junior's diagnosis. home.headline: Penn State week 5 injury report vs. Northwestern: Who’s in, who’s out, and who has to step up
home.blurb: It’s still early in the year, but the injury bug has already bitten Penn State hard, forcing star wide receiver Koby Howard to miss the start of conference play. Howard’s absence was significant in the Nittany Lions Week 4 loss to Wisconsin, and he’ll be out again on Friday night when Matt Campbell’s team helps open the newly rebuilt Ryan Field at Northwestern. Daryus Dixson still listed as questionable on Thursday night availability report Dixson did not leave the Week 4 loss to the Badgers, but according to Campbell, who addressed Dixson’s health on Wednesday, he was “dinged up” just before halftime. Dixson was on the initial injury report on Tuesday night, listed as “questionable,” and held the same status on Thursday night when the availability report was released about 24 hours before kickoff in Evanston. The return of Alex Tatsch, who missed Week 1 as he ramped up from an injury he suffered preparing for the Pinstripe Bowl in December, has helped to fill the void left by Smith and Kooper Ebel, and Tony Rojas has been rock-solid at the second level of D’Anton Lynn’s defense. Dixson is seemingly the only player on Penn State’s roster whose status is uncertain heading into Friday night. Considering he played through the injury in the second half against Wisconsin, his outlook appears favorable, but that he wasn’t upgraded to “probable” raises a legitimate question about whether or not he’ll be ready to suit up against the Wildcats. Notable Northwestern injuries: Luke Dehnicke still doubtful While not ruled out, Northwestern has two starters listed as doubtful for Friday night, including its second-leading receiver: tight end Luke Dehnicke. Dehnicke caught seven passes for 140 yards against Indiana in Week 4, but was banged up and could miss Week 5. The Wildcats may also be without starting defensive back Braden Turner. Fellow starting DB Damon Walters is listed as questionable. There’s another member of the 2025 recruiting class who has turned into a key cog for Penn State, whose situation is worth monitoring: cornerback Daryus Dixson. To get it, the Nittany Lions will need to be at full strength. Here’s a look at the injury report: Cam Smith is the notable downgrade from the early-week report. The redshirt freshman linebacker hasn’t played a defensive snap for the Nittany Lions since Week 1, and though he’s lower on a crowded linebacker depth chart, he’s a promising young player whom Campbell spoke highly of in the preseason.
